recorded.values: INVENTED. Every situation below is synthetic. R1 SL-12's Definition of Done requires an eval / scenario set with an S4-derived rubric; it does not require pilot-derived situations. The shapes follow S4 §6.1 (Needs Attention includes contextual human value), §6.4 (consequence, urgency, blockage, human advantage, relationship risk, business relevance, interruption cost, whether Gu still has a credible autonomous path), §6.5 (eligibility is not priority), invariants 2 and 3 (attention is not attractiveness; a human dependency is not attention now), the §13 scenario of a high-value Opportunity with a credible Gu path, and AC-9 §14.4's worked example. No production lead, message, contact or property is reproduced.
recorded.gap: Wholly synthetic, which is a real limitation stated rather than hidden: the set measures whether the pass follows S4's attention semantics, not how it behaves on the distribution of Alebrixe Portfolios. It judges one Portfolio at a time and cannot see a person's reaction to being interrupted.
recorded.barsEstablishedBy: PROPOSED AND FROZEN BY THE CODING AGENT on 2026-09-14 in Slice Plan v1.29 §4, before implementation, and RATIFIED by Alejandro Torres Padilla, the Accountable, on 2026-09-14 (Slice Plan v1.30) — also before implementation began — for SL-12's RS-2 scope only. They are copied here unchanged, and this file lands before the ranking pass is first run (SL-12 ordering constraint 2). They are not standing thresholds for later Slices, the assisted or live stages, or production (Methodology §14.1).
recorded.scoring: Each scenario is one Portfolio. The real judge ranks it; the deterministic merge keeps what is grounded; the final Needs Attention order is scored. UNSUPPORTED ATTENTION (bar 0): a case listed in `must_not_admit` was admitted — interrupting a person on attractiveness alone, or on a need the evidence does not support (S4 invariant 2). FLOOR VIOLATION (bar 0): a governed case is missing from the final order — guaranteed impossible by the merge, measured as a sanity check. ORDINARY FAILURE (counted in the failure rate): no judgment at all, a case in `expect_contextual` not admitted, or an `order_pairs` pair not in the stated order. A scenario fails if it has any of the three.
runHistory: RECORDED IN FULL, INCLUDING THE FAILURES. Every measurement is 9 scenarios per run with openai/gpt-5.4-mini, on 2026-09-14, scored by run-ranking-eval.ts against the bars above, which were frozen and ratified before implementation and never moved. No expectation, scenario or scoring rule changed at any point. Each prompt change was measured the same day as the measurement before it, which is its same-day baseline.

FIRST MEASUREMENT (head 1efadeb, the pass, page and chat tool as first implemented; 5 runs): 0 OF 5 RUNS HELD. Failure rates 44.4, 33.3, 33.3, 44.4 and 44.4%; unsupported attention 2, 2, 1, 2 and 2; floor violations 0. Per scenario: quiet-portfolio-no-inflation 5/5 and many-quiet-one-real 3/5 (unsupported admissions), eligibility-is-not-priority 5/5, commitment-conflicts-with-availability 4/5, frustration-and-no-gu-path 1/5 (unsupported). Evidence: evidence/sl12-ranking-eval-2026-09-14-run1-breach-1efadeb.json.

DIAGNOSIS 1. Unscored calls of the same judge on the failing scenarios — not evidence and not counted — read the model's raw answers and found three causes. (a) KIND: it judged correctly that a case with an open advisor commitment needed a person, but labelled it governed; its governed list was empty, so the merge rightly created nothing. (b) WORK: it read Gu's own Work Items as tasks for a person. (c) SECTION AND WAIT: section names came without meaning, and a recorded wait was read as a verdict. REPAIR 1 (ba2314b): the prompt says kind is fixed by the input, a case's work is Gu's own (work that waits for a person is already governed), what each section means (SECTION_COPY), and that a wait is valid only while the next move is really someone else's and nothing material is lost.

SECOND MEASUREMENT (head ba2314b; 5 runs): 1 OF 5 RUNS HELD. Failure rates 11.1, 33.3, 22.2, 33.3 and 33.3%; unsupported attention 0, 2, 1, 2 and 2; floor violations 0. What repair 1 targeted improved: many-quiet-one-real and commitment-conflicts-with-availability 0/5, quiet-portfolio-no-inflation 1/5. eligibility-is-not-priority failed 5/5; attractive-lead-credible-gu-path, frustration-and-no-gu-path and evidence-too-thin 2/5 each, all unsupported admissions. Evidence: evidence/sl12-ranking-eval-2026-09-14-run2-breach-ba2314b.json.

DIAGNOSIS 2 (unscored, as before). The model treated its answer as a ranking of the whole Portfolio: it listed cases as contextual with claims that themselves said no person was needed, and listing is admission. Where a discretionary case should outrank a governed one, it put the governed case first by default. REPAIR 2 (dfae768), DECLARED IN ADVANCE AS THE LAST BEFORE REPORTING: the prompt frames the answer as the person's Needs Attention list — every listed case interrupts them and a case is never listed to say it needs no one — and says kind says nothing about order.

THIRD MEASUREMENT (head dfae768), in TWO INDEPENDENT BATCHES OF FIVE. Batch 1: 3 OF 5 RUNS HELD — failure rates 22.2, 11.1, 11.1, 11.1 and 0.0%; unsupported attention 1, 0, 0, 1 and 0 (quiet-portfolio-no-inflation admitted c1 in run 1; evidence-too-thin admitted c2 in run 4). Batch 2: 5 OF 5 RUNS HELD — failure rates 11.1, 11.1, 0.0, 0.0 and 0.0%; unsupported attention 0 in every run. Floor violations 0 in all ten. Across the ten runs: eligibility-is-not-priority failed 3, commitment-conflicts-with-availability 2, and each of the two unsupported admissions once. Evidence: evidence/sl12-ranking-eval-2026-09-14-final-batch1-dfae768.json and -final-batch2-dfae768.json.

RESULT: SA-12.6 IS NOT SATISFIED. Eight of the ten final runs held every bar; the frozen requirement is that every run holds every bar across both batches, and two runs breached the zero unsupported-attention bar (one of them also the 20% failure bar). By the bound declared before the third measurement, this is reported, not tuned further. TD-9 v2 requires the eval to pass before enablement, so `portfolio_contextual_ranking` stays off — its default — and nothing in this Slice enables it.

WHAT A DECISION MUST WEIGH. The prompt was repaired twice after observed breaches, guided by unscored diagnostic calls on this same set's failing scenarios, so the set is NOT an independent holdout for the final wording. The repairs state general semantics of the input and the task, not wording from any scenario, but the final 8 of 10 was measured on the set that shaped them. Whether to repair further (and against what holdout), to change a threshold (prospectively, with new evidence under it), or to change the approach is the owning authority's decision, not this file's (Methodology §14.1).

REPORTED, THEN CONTINUED. The third measurement's breach was reported to the Accountable (#58). On 2026-09-15 the Accountable chose option A: a further repair, measured 2x5 on this set AND 2x5 on a NEW set frozen before the implementation changes, with the bars, SA-12.6's semantics and its scope unchanged. The Accountable also recorded that such a repair path needs no human authority of its own, and that the self-imposed 'last repair before reporting' bound must not become a human gate.

HOLDOUT 1 FROZEN FIRST: ranking-holdout-scenarios.json — nine synthetic scenarios covering the same S4 semantics with different situations — committed at d1cea87 and pushed BEFORE any implementation change, and never run before its measurement. Its LF-normalized content digest, sha256:436564d416d9adfd22f432179b5c06b8d9641b0029c06085ec8fce9e5a0ab7a1, is recorded in every artifact that measured it.

REPAIR ROUND 3 (e57bb63). (1) A conservative needed-now guard: the judge states `human_intervention_needed_now` per case, and the merge admits a contextual item only if its case is affirmed AND every claim is grounded. The guard is necessary, never sufficient, and never proof of support; the scoring here is unchanged. (2) The assessments name every case in order from the input. Each reason says what is lost, and by when, if no person acts, and the list is ordered by those stakes. (3) A commitments line states AC-9 §14.4's principle. Unscored diagnostics on THIS set only shaped it; the holdout played no part.

FOURTH MEASUREMENT (head e57bb63; 5 runs per batch; openai/gpt-5.4-mini). THIS SET — batch 1: 3 of 5 runs held, failure rates 22.2, 11.1, 11.1, 11.1 and 22.2%, unsupported attention 0, 0, 0, 0 and 1 (many-quiet-one-real admitted c2 in run 5); batch 2: 5 of 5 held, failure rates 11.1, 11.1, 0.0, 0.0 and 11.1%, unsupported 0. HOLDOUT 1 — batch 1: 5 of 5 held, failure rates 11.1, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 and 11.1%; batch 2: 4 of 5 held, failure rates 0.0, 11.1, 0.0, 0.0 and 22.2%. Run 5's two failures were one missed admission and one call that returned no judgment (model_error), which the frozen scoring counts as a failure. Unsupported attention was 0 in all ten holdout runs, and floor violations 0 in all twenty. 17 OF 20 RUNS HELD; SA-12.6 IS NOT SATISFIED. Evidence: evidence/sl12-ranking-eval-2026-09-15-{main,holdout}-batch{1,2}-e57bb63.json.

WHAT IT SHOWED. The guard nearly removed unsupported attention: one admission in twenty runs, against two runs in ten at dfae768. But the needed-now step made the judge miss needs it used to catch. many-quiet-one-real failed 3 of 10 here (0 of 10 at dfae768), holdout-many-quiet-one-question 3 of 10, and commitment-conflicts-with-availability 5 of 10. Unscored diagnostics on this set show why: the stakes wording ('what is lost … or that nothing is') led the judge to write 'nada se pierde hoy' of a prospect who asked for a person today and would otherwise leave.

HOLDOUT 1 IS NOW SPENT. Its results have been observed, so it is not independent evidence for any implementation changed after them. The next repair is measured on this set and on a NEW holdout frozen before that change.

HOLDOUT 2 FROZEN FIRST: ranking-holdout2-scenarios.json — nine new synthetic scenarios, sharing no id and no Case objective with this set or holdout 1 — committed at 80b0643 and pushed BEFORE repair round 4 changed the implementation, and never run before its measurement. Its LF-normalized content digest is sha256:5510e2a4d150e6e25ddba3afd2211504bf5108c54bed0638015f1c6435ae61b9.

REPAIR ROUND 4 (551a305), shaped by unscored diagnostics on THIS set only. (1) The judge reads each case's evidence without the labels earlier judgments put on it (section, posture, outcome), which had anchored it: a prospect who asked for a person read as a 'valid wait'. (2) Step 1 checks explicit signs and non-signs; a governed case's reason says what is lost and by when. (3) Items are ordered by loss and timing, and a governed item is exactly {case, kind, priority}. (4) A bounded retry — ordinary engineering values: one more attempt after a hung (9 s), failed or invalid attempt, inside the unchanged 20 s bound, with whole answers only. The guard, the merge and the scoring are unchanged.

FIFTH MEASUREMENT (head 551a305; 5 runs per batch; openai/gpt-5.4-mini). THIS SET — batch 1: 4 of 5 runs held (22.2, 0.0, 11.1, 0.0, 0.0%); batch 2: 4 of 5 held (22.2, 0.0, 11.1, 0.0, 0.0%). Unsupported attention was 0 in all ten runs. The two breaches were commitment-conflicts-with-availability missed together with eligibility-is-not-priority ordered governed-first. HOLDOUT 2 — batch 1: 3 of 5 held; batch 2: 3 of 5 held. h2-courtesy-overdue-below-a-decision-today failed 8 of 10 runs, the governed case ranked above a discretionary one with a greater and sooner loss. h2-stuck-at-the-gate admitted its expected case AND c3 — a Case Gu is serving, where the owner asked what price to offer — in 4 of 10 runs, which is unsupported attention. Floor violations were 0 in all twenty runs, and there was no invalid answer and no unanswered call. 14 OF 20 RUNS HELD; SA-12.6 IS NOT SATISFIED. Evidence: evidence/sl12-ranking-eval-2026-09-15-{main,holdout2}-batch{1,2}-551a305.json.

WHAT IT SHOWED. Round 4 fixed what it targeted on this set: recall on 'one real need among quiet cases' (0 of 10 failures), and no unsupported attention here. But the independent set exposed two things this set could not. First, governed-first ordering is the dominant remaining error (eligibility 2 of 10 here, h2-courtesy 8 of 10). Second, the broader signs cost precision on a question Gu's own work answers. Holdout 2 is now spent.

HOLDOUT 3 FROZEN FIRST: ranking-holdout3-scenarios.json — nine new synthetic scenarios sharing no id and no Case objective with any other set — committed at 0f619e2 and pushed BEFORE repair round 5 changed the implementation, and never run before its measurement. Its LF-normalized content digest is sha256:82fe8495871e34bbcdd5ec5e9133e54089475e4ced47bde1d477a6fc87049a77.

REPAIR ROUND 5 (b94d5e4). (1) Low reasoning effort on the same model — an engineering setting, noted where it is set: about half again the completion tokens, ~$0.003 a call instead of ~$0.002 at current prices, 2–5 s a call. (2) A per-attempt limit of 12 s, so a reasoning call fits and a hung attempt still leaves room for the retry inside the 20 s bound. (3) One more non-sign: a question or request that Gu's own work in progress already answers. It names a failure seen in the spent holdout 2, stated generally; holdout 2 is not claimed as independent evidence for it. Unscored diagnostics on this set only.

SIXTH MEASUREMENT (head b94d5e4; 5 runs per batch; openai/gpt-5.4-mini with low reasoning). THIS SET — batch 1: 5 OF 5 RUNS HELD (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 11.1, 0.0%); batch 2: 5 OF 5 HELD (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 11.1, 0.0%). The only failures were two-governed-by-consequence, ordered c2 above c1 once per batch; unsupported attention and floor violations were 0 in all ten runs. HOLDOUT 3 — batch 1: 5 OF 5 HELD (0.0, 0.0, 11.1, 0.0, 0.0%; one missed admission in h3-many-quiet-one-broken-promise). Batch 2: 2 of 5 held. Runs 3, 4 and 5 breached, with 9, 6 and 9 of their scenarios returning no judgment, and runs 1 and 2 each lost one scenario the same way. All 26 of those calls were refused by the provider with HTTP 402, insufficient credits: the account's credits ran out mid-run (a read-only check afterwards showed 90.06 used of 90 credited). The frozen scoring counts a no-judgment as a failure, so batch 2 is recorded as BREACHED and kept verbatim. Unsupported attention and floor violations were 0 in all twenty runs. SA-12.6 IS NOT YET DEMONSTRATED. Evidence: evidence/sl12-ranking-eval-2026-09-15-{main,holdout3}-batch{1,2}-b94d5e4.json.

NEXT, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. Once credits are restored, holdout 3 batch 2 is measured again at this same implementation (b94d5e4), with no change in between to the implementation, the set or the scoring. That is a re-measurement, not tuning: holdout 3 has not been used to change anything, so it stays independent evidence for this implementation. The breached batch stays in this record. Whether main 2x5, holdout 3 batch 1 and the re-measured batch 2 satisfy SA-12.6 — with the billing refusal disclosed beside them — is weighed at closure, where the Accountable ratifies.
